newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane, LPGs jump on bullish stock data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane, LPGs jump on bullish stock data.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices continued to rally on Monday, fueled by a report that showed propane stocks declined last month, industry sources said.
In the American Petroleum Institute report released late Friday, propane rose about 2.5 million barrels last month to a current total of about 49.46 million barrels, players said.
The build was mostly at the expense of the U.S. Gulf Coast, which showed an unexpected 137,000-barrel draw. The Conway, Kansas, hub in the Midwest had a 1.4 million barrel build, traders said.
Propane stocks traditionally rise in summer months.

The delayed reaction to the news pushed prices at Mont Belvieu, Texas, to 50.75 cents a gallon, up almost one cent from Friday's levels. Conway propane also jumped, with barrels priced at 51 cents a gallon.
But traders noted that trade was only moderately active, with players squaring end-September positions. An industry function in Tulsa, Okla., also limited dealings.
Other LPG products were also stronger on the bullish stock data. Ethane stocks fell 416,000 barrels in August, about one-half the normal build for this time of year.
Total U.S. ethane stocks as of Aug. 31 stood at 14.56 million, 11.7 million barrels below levels last year.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
